t.7.27.1: Then, having crossed over Kailāsa, the ten-necked Daśagrīva, the mighty and splendid night-wanderer, together with his Rākṣasas, reached the world of Indra.
t.7.27.2: The din of that Rākṣasa army, which was about to advance from every side, rose to the world of the gods, like the roar of an ocean being split asunder.
t.7.27.3: But Indra, hearing that Rāvaṇa had arrived, his throne shaken, spoke there to all those gods who had assembled.
t.7.27.4: He addressed the Ādityas together with the Vasus, the Rudras, the Viśvas, the Sādhyas and the hosts of Maruts: "Make yourselves ready for battle against the evil-souled Rāvaṇa."
t.7.27.5: Thus addressed by Śakra, the gods, equal to Śakra in battle, mighty in strength and filled with eagerness for combat, armed themselves.
t.7.27.6: But the great Indra, dejected and terrified on account of Rāvaṇa, came into the presence of Viṣṇu and spoke these words.
t.7.27.7: O Viṣṇu, you of great valour and prowess, what shall we do? For that mighty rākṣasa is advancing toward us for battle.
t.7.27.8: He is mighty through the granting of a boon, and truly by no other cause. And that word of Prajāpati must indeed be made true, O god.
t.7.27.10: O god of great might, O best of beings, in times of distress there is no other refuge or final resort for the gods except you.
t.7.27.9: Therefore, just as Namuci, Vṛtra, Bali, Naraka and Śambara were burned up by relying on your counsel, so act now.
t.7.27.11: For you are Nārāyaṇa, the glorious, lotus-naveled, eternal one; and it is by you that I have been established in the eternal kingship of the gods.
t.7.27.12: Tell me that truly yourself, O god of gods: will you, with sword and discus as your aids, fight the enemy in battle?
t.7.27.14: This wicked one cannot, for now, be slain in battle by the gods and Dānavas, even when they encounter him, for by virtue of the granted boon he is hard to conquer.
t.7.27.13: Thus addressed by Śakra, the lord god Nārāyaṇa said: "You need not be alarmed; now hear what I have to say."
t.7.27.15: In any case, that Rākṣasa, formidable in strength and with his son as his ally, will accomplish a mighty deed; this is evident from his very nature.
t.7.27.16: As for what you say to me, Śakra, that I will fight in battle, I shall not fight against that Rāvaṇa, the lord of the rākṣasas.
t.7.27.17: Viṣṇu never turns back without slaying his enemy; yet this desire is hard to fulfil today against the rākṣasa, since he has obtained a boon.
t.7.27.19: I shall slay this Rāvaṇa together with his son in battle; knowing that the time has come, I shall gladden the gods.
t.7.27.18: I promise you in your presence, O lord of the gods, O Śatakratu: I myself shall be the cause of this rākṣasa's death.
t.7.27.20: Meanwhile, as the night was drawing to its close, a roar was heard on every side from that army of Rāvaṇa, which had joined in battle.
t.7.27.21: Then a terrible battle arose between the gods and the rākṣasas, filled with a tumultuous roar and fought with weapons of many kinds.
t.7.27.22: Meanwhile, at Rāvaṇa's command, his ministers, valiant rākṣasas of terrible appearance, rushed forward to do battle.
t.7.27.23: Mārīca and Prahasta, Mahāpārśva and Mahodara, Akampana and Nikumbha, Śuka and Sāraṇa as well.
t.7.27.24: Saṃhrādi and Dhūmaketu, Mahādaṃṣṭra and Mahāmukha, Jambumālī, Mahāmālī, and the Rākṣasa Virūpākṣa.
t.7.27.25: Surrounded by all these warriors of great valor, Sumālī, bull among Rākṣasas and maternal grandfather of Rāvaṇa, entered the army.
t.7.27.26: For he, greatly enraged, together with those night-rangers, is destroying all the hosts of the gods with sharp weapons of many kinds.
t.7.27.27: Meanwhile the heroic Vasu, the eighth of the Vasus, renowned by the name Sāvitra, entered the great battle.
t.7.27.29: Then those valiant Rākṣasas struck down by hundreds of thousands those gods standing in the battle, with terrible weapons of many kinds.
t.7.27.28: Then a battle broke out between the gods and the Rākṣasas, a battle that won fame for the enraged Rakṣases, who never turn back in combat.
t.7.27.30: But the gods, by their own splendour and with weapons of many kinds, sent the terrible and mighty Rākṣasas to the abode of Yama in battle.
t.7.27.31: Meanwhile the valiant rākṣasa named Sumālī, enraged, advanced into the battle with weapons of many kinds.
t.7.27.32: Enraged, he scatters that entire army of the gods with sharpened weapons of many kinds, as the wind scatters the clouds.
t.7.27.33: Tormented by great showers of arrows and by dreadful spears and lances, all those gods could not stand firm and composed.
t.7.27.34: Then, as the thirty gods were being put to flight by Sumālin, Sāvitra, the eighth god of the Vasus, stood his ground.
t.7.27.35: But the greatly radiant one, surrounded by his own troops, held back with his valor the night-roaming demon who was striking out in the battle.
t.7.27.36: Between those two, greatly frenzied, Sumālin and the Vasu, who never turned back in battles, there arose a fight most dreadful in the world.
t.7.27.37: Then, with mighty arrows, the most great-souled Vasu brought down in an instant that great serpent-drawn chariot of his.
t.7.27.38: Having destroyed his chariot in battle with hundreds of sharp arrows, Vasu seized a mace in his hand for the purpose of slaying him.
t.7.27.39: Swiftly seizing that blazing, splendid weapon, which resembled the rod of Kāla, Sāvitra brought it crashing down upon the head of Sumāli.
t.7.27.40: Falling then upon his head, it blazed with the radiance of a fiery meteor, like a great thunderbolt hurled by Sahasrākṣa upon a mountain.
t.7.27.41: Then neither his bone nor body nor flesh was to be seen; struck down by the mace in that battle, he had been reduced to ashes.
t.7.27.42: Seeing him slain in battle, all those Rākṣasas on every side fled together, crying out with a great clamour.
